items.author: Aidan Mackenzie
items.title: Senator Merkley’s sign is false BAAJA does not “lock in” projects, it requires agencies to identify specific conditions before revoking permits (illegality is covered) Few data centers even require federal permits — BAAJA’s main effect is making data centers pay more!
items.summary: Mackenzie disputes a sign Sen. Merkley displayed while speaking against BAAJA on the floor on November 18, saying the bill does not lock in projects.

quote.text: Few data centers even require federal permits — BAAJA’s main effect is making data centers pay more!
quote.speaker: Aidan Mackenzie

items.title: Senate continues work today on bipartisan legislation to reform the federal permitting process for energy and infrastructure projects.

items.author: Joshua Siegel
items.title: SCOOP: Senate permitting reform negotiators have finalized changes to BAAJA ahead of the final vote expected this week.
items.summary: Siegel reports the four negotiators have finalized a managers' amendment with compromise tribal and NHPA changes and tweaks to landowner compensation for transmission.

quote.text: I obtained the new managers' amendment text.
quote.speaker: Joshua Siegel

items.author: Joshua Siegel
items.title: Scoop in @PunchbowlNews AM: Senate negotiators near deal on changes to NHPA section of BAAJA to shore up votes amid tribal pushback.
items.summary: Siegel reports negotiators are close to an NHPA change led by Sens. Murkowski and Schatz that requires NHPA review for certain federally funded projects.

quote.text: The change specifies that certain projects receiving federal funding have to go through NHPA reviews.
quote.speaker: Joshua Siegel

items.author: Joshua Siegel
items.title: More in PM: EPW ranker Sen. Whitehouse told me the 4 negotiators plan to oppose the standalone amendments that get floor votes even if they agree w/underlying policy in order to uphold the deal.
items.summary: Siegel reports Whitehouse says the four sponsors will vote against standalone floor amendments to protect the deal.

quote.text: That’s pretty standard on bipartisan bills that the sponsors stand by the bill.
quote.speaker: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse, as quoted by Joshua Siegel

items.author: Joshua Siegel
items.title: On the second round of managers amendment changes to the bill that are expected, Sen. Whitehouse told me it would be a mix of “technical things that are actually technical improvements and bipartisan things that can move smoothly.”
items.summary: Siegel reports Whitehouse expects a second managers' amendment mixing technical edits and bipartisan changes.

quote.text: technical things that are actually technical improvements and bipartisan things that can move smoothly
quote.speaker: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse, as quoted by Joshua Siegel

items.author: Joshua Siegel

quote.text: finishing up the hotline on amendments and hoping to get agreement there

items.author: Joshua Siegel
items.title: Update: Sen. Schiff is still “pushing for consideration of his amendment via a floor vote prior to final passage of the bill” to strip NHPA section of BAAJA, a spokesman told me “The amendment is strictly germane…and has the support of two-thirds of the Democratic Caucus”
items.summary: Siegel reports Sen. Schiff is pushing for a floor vote on an amendment to strip the NHPA section, which his office says two-thirds of Democrats support.

quote.text: The amendment is strictly germane…and has the support of two-thirds of the Democratic Caucus
quote.speaker: Spokesman for Sen. Adam Schiff, as quoted by Joshua Siegel

items.author: Aidan Mackenzie
items.title: Pretty big news: the funding for the Historic Preservation Fund has been increased from $200M per year to $300M per year!

quote.text: The fund exists to support state and Tribal review and consultation, allowing better quality review to get done faster
quote.speaker: Aidan Mackenzie

items.author: David Pomerantz
items.title: No substantive changes to transmission here.

quote.speaker: David Pomerantz
